title: Long words, syllable by syllable
goal: Any word can be typed from its sound: one syllable per stroke, split where you hear a break, the join key on every stroke after the first.

items: Say the word slowly and split it where you hear a break.
Strike each syllable like a one-syllable word (lesson 7).
Hold the join key on every stroke after the first.

blocks.x: Without `+`, each stroke is a word of its own (*column*, *prah*, *meyez*). The join key is the whole point.

items: **A weak last syllable drops its vowel**, exactly like an ending: [[table|TAEU/+-BL]], [[lemon|HRE/+PH-PB]].

**A weak vowel you do strike is `U`** (a weak short i is `EU`) as you hear it, **or the letter the word spells it with**: *profitable* is [[profitable|PRAF/+U/+TU/+-BL]] and [[profitable|PRAF/+O/+TO/+-BL]].
**A weak last syllable that fits on the stroke before it can fold onto it**: [[sensible|SEPB/+SU/+-BL]] or [[sensible|SEPB/+SUBL]].

blocks.x: Split anywhere you hear a break

There is more than one right answer, and every one is in the dictionary. *lem-on* is [[lemon|HREPL/+UPB]] and *le-mon* is [[lemon|HRE/+PHUPB]]. *compromise* can be *com-pro-mise*, [[compromise|KOPL/+PR/+PHAOEUZ]] (*comp-ro-mise*) or [[compromise|KOPL/+PROPL/+AOEUZ]] (*compro-mise*). Any run of consonants that can start a syllable may go to the next stroke, or stay.

A stroke is any run of sounds with one vowel at most, so three, four, five, six strokes all work: *complete* is [[complete|KU/+PH/+HRAOET]], [[complete|K/+UPL/+PHRAOET]], [[complete|KU/+-PL/+-P/+HRAOET]]. The cheapest few of each length are in the dictionary. Use fewer strokes when you can.
This is why you are never stuck. If a word has no memorised outline, say it and strike its syllables. Every word of two syllables or more in the dictionary can be reached at least one of these ways.

opts: the join key `+` on strokes 2 and 3
blocks.why: It is [[PHU/+SHE/+TAOE]]. Without the `+`, each stroke would be a separate word.
